 K-drama's beloved duo Yoo Yeon-seok, Seo Hyeon-jin reunites after 10 years
 Published : Oct. 31, 2026 - 16:00:05
 Add The Korea Herald on Google
 Bookmark Event 
 Link copied!
 Lee Yoon-seo 
Covering TV, streaming, esports and the business and cultural trends shaping Korean entertainment
 Subscribe + 
 'The Perfect Lie' faces SBS' ratings hit 'Doctor X: Mafia in White' in a fierce weekend drama showdown
 "The Perfect Lie," starring Yoo Yeon-seok (MBC) It took a decade, but one of K-drama’s most beloved on-screen pairings is back.
 After winning over audiences with their signature bickering banter in the 2016 ratings smash "Dr. Romantic," Yoo Yeon-seok and Seo Hyeon-jin are joining forces again, this time in a psychological thriller steeped in lies and suspicion.
 The long-awaited small-screen reunion took center stage at a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday to promote the new series, "The Perfect Lie," where Yoo reflected on how effortlessly the two rekindled their rapport after 10 years apart.
 "Fans had been hoping for years that Seo and I would work together again, so reuniting after 10 years feels especially meaningful," Yoo said.
 "The first days on set are usually nerve-racking or awkward, but this time I found myself thinking, 'Why is filming so much fun?'" he said. "We know each other so well that working together was genuinely thrilling and exciting."
 Helmed by director Cho Young-min, best known for his delicate character studies in "Do You Like Brahms?" and "You and Everything Else," "The Perfect Lie" marks the filmmaker's first foray into high-concept suspense.
 The narrative kicks off when surgeon Min Joon-ho (Yoo) and elementary school teacher Kang Ji-seon (Seo) share a seemingly routine first date, only to find themselves ensnared in a mysterious incident the following day. As their accounts of the night diverge, the series devolves into a tense psychological mind game, challenging the audience to figure out who to trust.
 Explaining his decision to cast Yoo and Seo as the two main anchors for the story, Cho pointed to their ability to project contrasting dimensions within a single character.
 "This story needed actors who could embody two opposing faces — one you instinctively want to trust and another capable of concealing a lie. I was confident both could bring that duality to their performances," Cho said.
 "For example, Yoo is an adaptable actor who can instantly absorb and respond to direction, while Seo has such compelling emotional depth that you naturally find yourself wanting to believe whatever she says," Cho said.
 "The Perfect Lie," starring Seo Hyeon-jin (MBC) For Yoo, a veteran of 23 years whose resume includes hits like "Reply 1994" and "Mr. Sunshine," the project serves as a commentary on how personal biases can distort reality.
 "Someone's truth can be distorted by their image, reputation or the judgments others make about them. And sometimes, we end up believing those distortions. Those were the questions I kept in mind while filming," Yoo said.
 Seo echoed those sentiments, describing the series as an exploration of the subjective standards people apply when deciding what to believe.
 "Our drama is fundamentally about lies," Seo said. "It asks what criteria people use to believe a lie and, perhaps more importantly, what they want to believe. The story approaches those questions from many different perspectives."
 Meanwhile, the series arrives amid fierce competition in the weekend television lineup.
 "The Perfect Lie," which premieres Friday on MBC and will air Fridays and Saturdays, enters a crowded field that includes SBS' medical drama "Doctor X: Mafia in White," which has a peak viewership rating of 19.5 percent.
 Asked about the ratings rivalry, Yoo acknowledged the competitive landscape but expressed confidence that the show's distinct genre would help cut through the noise.
 "The competition across Friday-Saturday and Saturday-Sunday dramas is fierce," Yoo said. "But our drama belongs to a different genre."
 "As a psychological thriller, it invites viewers to pay close attention to the characters' subtle emotional shifts, psychological mind games and conflicting claims about the truth," Yoo added. "I think that suspense will leave audiences eager to tune in every week to find out what happens next."
 Yoo Yeon-seok (left) and Seo Hyeon-jin pose for a photo during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday. (MBC)
